href=\"#svg-toc\"></use></svg></span>\n          </label>\n        </div>\n        <article role=\"main\" id=\"furo-main-content\">\n          <section id=\"guidelines-for-using-ai-tools\">\n<span id=\"generative-ai\"></span><span id=\"ai-tools\"></span><h1>Guidelines for using AI tools<a class=\"headerlink\" href=\"#guidelines-for-using-ai-tools\" title=\"Link to this heading\">¶</a></h1>\n<p>The person submitting an issue or PR is responsible for its content,\nregardless of whether AI tools were used in its creation. Generative AI\ntools can produce output quickly, but discretion, good judgment, and\ncritical thinking are the foundation of all good contributions. We value\ngood code, concise accurate documentation, and well scoped PRs without\nunneeded code churn.</p>\n<section id=\"considerations-for-success\">\n<h2>Considerations for success<a class=\"headerlink\" href=\"#considerations-for-success\" title=\"Link to this heading\">¶</a></h2>\n<p>Authors must review the work done by AI tooling in detail to ensure it\nactually makes sense before proposing it as a PR or filing it as an issue.</p>\n<p>We expect PR authors and those filing issues to be able to explain their\nproposed changes in their own words.</p>\n<p>Disclosure of the use of AI tools in the PR description is appreciated,\nwhile not required. Be prepared to explain how the tool was used and what\nchanges it made.</p>\n<p>Whether you are using AI tools or not, keep the following principles in\nmind for the quality of your contribution:</p>\n<ul class=\"simple\">\n<li><p>Consider whether the change is necessary</p></li>\n<li><p>Make minimal, focused changes</p></li>\n<li><p>Follow existing coding style and patterns</p></li>\n<li><p>Write tests that exercise the change</p></li>\n<li><p>Keep backwards compatibility with prior releases in mind. Existing\ntests may be ensuring specific API behaviors are maintained.</p></li>\n</ul>\n<p>Pay close attention to AI generated recommendations for testing changes.\nProvide input about Python’s testing principles when guiding an AI model.\nAlways review the output before opening a pull request or issue,\nincluding proposed PR or issue titles and descriptions.</p>\n</section>\n<section id=\"acceptable-uses\">\n<h2>Acceptable uses<a class=\"headerlink\" href=\"#acceptable-uses\" title=\"Link to this heading\">¶</a></h2>\n<p>Some of the acceptable uses of generative AI include:</p>\n<ul class=\"simple\">\n<li><p>Assistance with writing comments, especially in a non-native language</p></li>\n<li><p>Gaining understanding of existing code</p></li>\n<li><p>Supplementing contributor knowledge for code, tests, and documentation</p></li>\n</ul>\n</section>\n<section id=\"unacceptable-uses\">\n<h2>Unacceptable uses<a class=\"headerlink\" href=\"#unacceptable-uses\" title=\"Link to this heading\">¶</a></h2>\n<p>Maintainers may close issues and PRs that are not useful or productive,\nwithout explanation, regardless of whether AI tools were used or not.</p>\n<p>If a contributor repeatedly opens unproductive issues or PRs, they may be\nblocked from contributing to the project because it is disruptive and\ndisrespectful of the maintainers time.</p>\n<p>It is not acceptable to alter or bypass existing tests, or remove desired\nfunctionality, in order to make a failing test pass. Such changes are not\na real fix.</p>\n</section>\n<section id=\"how-these-guidelines-are-applied\">\n<h2>How these guidelines are applied<a class=\"headerlink\" href=\"#how-these-guidelines-are-applied\" title=\"Link to this heading\">¶</a></h2>\n<p>Using AI tools is not a reason on its own for an issue or PR to be labeled\nor closed. When a maintainer thinks an issue or PR does not follow these\nguidelines, they may apply one of the following labels. A bot then posts a\ncomment that links to this page.</p>\n<ul class=\"simple\">\n<li><p><a class=\"extlink-gh-label reference external\" href=\"https://github.com/python/cpython/labels/AI-needs-explanation\">AI-needs-explanation</a>: the issue or PR stays open. Reply in your\nown words: explain what the change does or what the issue is about, and\ndescribe how you checked that it is correct.</p></li>\n<li><p><a class=\"extlink-gh-label reference external\" href=\"https://github.com/python/cpython/labels/AI-guidelines-not-met\">AI-guidelines-not-met</a>: the issue or PR is closed. If you think\nwe misunderstood your contribution, reply on the issue or PR. You are\nwelcome to explain your approach or ask questions about these guidelines.</p></li>\n</ul>\n</section>\n</section>\n\n        </article>\n      </div>\n      <footer>\n        \n        <div Uploads under a reserved prefix require\n+an active grant, repositories expose the grants through version 1.5 of\n+the JSON Simple API, and installers can admit only dependencies inside\n+granted namespaces.\n+\n+All names are :ref:`normalized <packagenamespaces-naming>` before they\n+are compared, and grants never cross repositories: a grant on one index\n+confers nothing on a mirror.\n+\n+.. _packagenamespaces-naming:\n+\n+Naming\n+------\n+\n+.. function:: normalize_name(name)\n+\n+   Return the normalized form of *name*: every run of ``-``, ``_`` and\n+   ``.`` becomes a single ``-`` and the result is lowercased.\n+\n+.. function:: is_valid_namespace(name)\n+\n+   Return true if *name* is a valid namespace: a non-empty string with\n+   ASCII letters or digits at both ends.\n+\n+.. function:: hyphen_depth(name)\n+\n+   Return the number of hyphens in the normalized form of *name*.\n+\n+.. function:: namespace_matches(namespace, project)\n+\n+   Return true if *project* exactly matches *namespace* or starts with\n+   it followed by a hyphen, after normalizing both.\n+\n+Semantics\n+---------\n+\n+.. data:: DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT\n+\n+   The default cap on hyphens per namespace: ``3``.  ``None`` disables\n+   the limit.\n+\n+.. function:: grants_overlap(first, second)\n+\n+   Return true if two namespaces overlap.  Both are normalized, a hyphen\n+   is appended to each, and the comparison runs in both directions.\n+\n+.. class:: GrantStore(depth_limit=DEFAULT_DEPTH_LIMIT)\n+\n+   The active grants of one repository.\n+\n+   .. method:: reserve(namespace, owner)\n+\n+      Reserve *namespace* for *owner*.  Raises\n+      :exc:`InvalidNamespaceError`, :exc:`DepthLimitError` or\n+      :exc:`OverlapError`.  A namespace overlapping an existing grant\n+      may only be reserved by that grant's owner.\n+\n+   .. method:: transfer(namespace, new_owner)\n+\n+      Move a grant to a new owner.\n+\n+   .. method:: remove(namespace)\n+\n+      Remove a grant and return it.\n+\n+   .. method:: get(namespace)\n+\n+      Return the grant for *namespace*, or None.\n+\n+   .. method:: namespaces()\n+\n+      Return every granted namespace, sorted.\n+\n+   .. method:: matching(project)\n+\n+      Return the grants matching *project*, sorted by name.\n+\n+   .. method:: parent(namespace)\n+\n+      Return the granted parent of *namespace*, or None.\n+\n+   .. method:: children(namespace)\n+\n+      Return the granted direct children of *namespace*, sorted.\n+\n+.. class:: Grant\n+\n+   A reservation with :attr:`name` and :attr:`owner` attributes.\n+\n+.. exception:: GrantError\n+\n+   Base class for grant-store errors.\n+\n+.. exception:: InvalidNamespaceError\n+\n+   A namespace is not a valid project name.\n+\n+.. exception:: OverlapError\n+\n+   A namespace overlaps a grant held by another owner.\n+\n+.. exception:: DepthLimitError\n+\n+   A namespace exceeds the hyphen depth limit.\n+\n+.. exception:: UnknownGrantError\n+\n+   No active grant exists for a namespace.\n+\n+Uploads\n+-------\n+\n+.. data:: CONFLICT_STATUS\n+\n+   The HTTP status for a refused upload: ``409``.\n+\n+.. exception:: UploadConflictError\n+\n+   An upload matched a reserved namespace without a grant.
